title: Kailix's Peabody buy fits a niche commodities playbook
content:
On April 30, 2026, Kailix Advisors LLC disclosed a new position in Peabody Energy(NYSE:BTU), acquiring 239,800 shares in an estimated $8.38 million trade based on quarterly average pricing.

Kailix Advisors initiated a 239,800-share stake in Peabody Energy(NYSE:BTU); estimated transaction value is $8.38 million based on quarterly average price. The quarter-end value of the BTU holding rose by $7.90 million, reflecting both the position establishment and price movement during the period. The BTU trade represented a 7.33% change in reportable assets under management. Post-trade, the fund held 239,800 shares valued at $7.90 million. BTU accounts for 6.91% of fund AUM, placing it outside Kailix Advisors’ top five holdings.

What happened

According to its April 30, 2026, SEC filing, Kailix Advisors LLC established a new position in Peabody Energy(NYSE:BTU) by acquiring 239,800 shares. The estimated transaction value is $8.38 million, calculated from the mean unadjusted closing price during the first quarter of 2026. At quarter-end, the BTU stake was valued at $7.90 million, reflecting both the initial purchase and subsequent price changes during the period.

What else to know

Kailix Advisors’ new BTU stake accounted for 6.91% of its $114.34 million reportable assets under management as of March 31, 2026. Top holdings after the filing:

NYSE: DCH: $26.39 million (23.1% of AUM) NASDAQ: GPRE: $17.30 million (15.1% of AUM) NYSE: CSTM: $13.52 million (11.8% of AUM) NYSE: WTTR: $13.16 million (11.5% of AUM) NYSE: AMRZ: $10.27 million (9.0% of AUM) As of April 29, 2026, Peabody Energy shares were priced at $27.44, up 117.1% over the past year, outperforming the S&P 500 by 88.76 percentage points.

Company/Etf overview

Metric Value Revenue (TTM) $3.86 billion Net income (TTM) ($52.90 million) Dividend yield 1.13% Price (as of market close April 29, 2026) $27.44

Company snapshot

BTU produces and sells thermal and metallurgical coal, supplying electricity generators, industrial facilities, and steel manufacturers across the United States and internationally. It operates through mining, preparation, and sale of coal, with revenue primarily generated from coal sales and trading, as well as transportation-related services. Its main customer base includes electric utilities, steel producers, and industrial clients in North America, Asia, and other global markets.

Peabody Energy is a leading coal producer with a diversified portfolio of mining operations in the United States and Australia. The company leverages its extensive coal reserves and integrated supply chain to serve both thermal and metallurgical coal markets. Its scale and international reach position it as a key supplier to major power and industrial customers worldwide.

Story Continues

What this transaction means for investors

Kailix Advisors isn't a megafund slotting Peabody Energy into a broad book. The whole portfolio is $114 million across 10 names, and almost every one is a commodity, materials, or industrial play — Constellium aluminum, Green Plains ethanol, Lithium Americas, Select Water Solutions oilfield services, Amrize cement. Adding a coal producer at roughly 7% of AUM doesn't change the character of the fund. It reinforces it. There's also no public statement on rationale, so anything beyond "they liked it enough to make it a top-six position" is reading tea leaves. The distinction for anyone weighing a coal trade off this filing: Kailix is a niche manager building a thematic book, not a benchmark-aware megafund signaling a sector-wide call. A 7% slot here is one specialist's opinion, not the institutional consensus an "X bought Y" headline can imply.

Generates revenue through the design, engineering, and manufacture of automotive driveline and metal forming products, serving both OEM and industrial customers. Primary customers include manufacturers of light trucks, SUVs, passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial equipment.

title: Constellium SE (CSTM) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Record Growth and Strategic Initiatives ...
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Revenue: $2.5 billion, a 24% increase compared to Q1 2025. Net Income: $196 million, up from $38 million in Q1 2025. Adjusted EBITDA: $359 million, a 93% increase from Q1 2025. Adjusted EBITDA (excluding metal price lag): $262 million, up 78% from $147 million in Q1 2025. Free Cash Flow: $5 million for the quarter. Share Repurchase: $28 million returned to shareholders through repurchase of 1.2 million shares. Shipments: 370,000 tons in the first quarter. Net Debt: $1.8 billion, stable compared to the end of 2025. Leverage: Reduced to 2.2 times at the end of the quarter. Liquidity: $904 million as of the end of the first quarter. A&T Segment Adjusted EBITDA: $102 million, a 24% increase from Q1 2025. PARP Segment Adjusted EBITDA: $151 million, a 152% increase from Q1 2025. AS&I Segment Adjusted EBITDA: $24 million, a 50% increase from Q1 2025.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with KOF. Is CSTM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: April 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Constellium SE (NYSE:CSTM) reported record adjusted EBITDA for the first quarter of 2026, with a 93% increase compared to the previous year. The company raised its full-year outlook, expecting 2026 to be a record year for both adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow. Revenue increased by 24% year-over-year, driven by higher revenue per ton and favorable metal prices. Net income rose significantly to $196 million from $38 million in the same quarter last year, attributed to higher gross profit and favorable changes in other gains and losses. Constellium SE (NYSE:CSTM) announced a new $300 million share repurchase program, reflecting confidence in its financial position and commitment to returning value to shareholders.

Negative Points

Shipments in the PARP and AS&I segments were lower, offsetting higher shipments in the A&T segment. The company faces inflationary pressures in freight, lubricants, and coatings, which could impact costs. The conflict in the Middle East presents uncertainties, particularly regarding metal supply and energy costs. Automotive demand in Europe remains weak, especially in the premium vehicle segment, affecting the company's performance in this market. The company anticipates higher costs in the second half of the year due to annual maintenance outages, which could impact profitability.

Q & A Highlights

Q: Can you discuss the expected cadence for 2026, particularly between the second quarter and the second half of the year? Also, how should we think about 2027 and 2028 in terms of EBITDA? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: Traditionally, the first half of the year is stronger due to seasonality, with the second quarter being particularly strong in packaging. Higher costs are expected in the second half due to annual maintenance outages. Jack Guo, CFO: Q2 is expected to be the strongest quarter. For 2027, it's a transition year with ramp-ups in recycling and casting projects. We expect strength in aerospace and TID North America, but automotive may remain weak, especially in Europe.

Story Continues

Q: Regarding aerospace, can you talk about expectations for volume versus high margins for the rest of the year? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: We recently announced a multiyear contract with Airbus for various extruded products, including our Airware aluminum-lithium technology. This contract strengthens our relationship with Airbus and supports a strong mix for our extrusion business.

Q: What does your guidance assume for scrap spreads for the rest of the year? A: Jack Guo, CFO: For Q2, scrap spreads are locked in and more favorable than Q1. Over 50% of our needs for the second half are secured. The market remains volatile, and our guidance assumes a middle-of-the-road approach for the second half, which is above prior expectations but not as aggressive as the first half of 2026.

Q: Is there an opportunity to accelerate share buybacks given the increase in free cash flow? A: Jack Guo, CFO: We maintain a balanced approach to capital allocation. We are comfortable with the current pace of our $300 million buyback program over three years and view buying back shares as attractive.

Q: How do recent changes in Section 232 derivative tariffs impact your business? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: The recent changes have a minor impact on our AS&I business. Overall, tariffs are expected to stick, and we anticipate continued indirect benefits from Section 232.

Q: Can you expand on the impact of the automotive market, particularly in Europe and the US? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: In Europe, BYD's production is more steel-focused, so we don't expect much impact. In the US, we benefit from the outage of a competitor's facility, which is expected to continue. AS&I is impacted by slower production ramp-ups, but the financial impact is minor.

Q: Is there potential to increase the proportion of products made from scrap given current market conditions? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: We are already using significant scrap across our operations and are focused on optimizing metal costs through increased scrap usage. Jack Guo, CFO: Recycling and casting are core to our operations, and we are investing in these areas to enhance our capabilities.

Q: Can you quantify your ability to expand recycling given potential shortages in billet and tight markets? A: Ingrid Joerg, CEO: The shortage of primary aluminum isn't the main driver for us. We focus on using available scrap in the market, which is volatile. Our goal is to optimize metal costs by replacing prime metal with scrap, depending on availability.

title: Constellium SE Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Constellium SE Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Record adjusted EBITDA was primarily driven by a unique convergence of supply shortages in North American automotive rolled products and highly favorable scrap spreads. The company is leveraging a competitor's facility outage in North America to maximize its own capacity and gain new customer qualifications in the automotive sector. Aerospace performance reached a first-quarter record, supported by record commercial aircraft backlogs and easing destocking trends in the supply chain. Management attributes margin expansion to improved productivity in recycling and casting operations, which allowed for better capture of historically wide scrap spreads. The business model's pass-through structure effectively minimized exposure to primary aluminum price volatility, focusing performance on operational execution and mix. Strategic onshoring trends in the U.S. are driving increased demand for Transportation, Industry, and Defense (TID) products, offsetting some industrial weakness in Europe.

2026 Outlook and 2028 Strategic Roadmap

Full-year 2026 guidance assumes that favorable market dynamics, including automotive supply shortages and scrap spread benefits, will persist through the year. Management views 2027 as a 'transition year' characterized by the ramp-up of major recycling and casting investments at Neuf-Brisach and Muscle Shoals. The 2028 target of $900 million adjusted EBITDA is built on structural improvements and does not rely on the current temporary favorable scrap environment. Guidance for the second half of 2026 incorporates a 'middle of the road' approach for scrap spreads, acknowledging high volatility and less aggressive assumptions than the first half. Capital allocation will prioritize a balanced approach between a new $300 million share repurchase program and gross debt reduction.

Risk Factors and Macroeconomic Context

The conflict in the Middle East is creating inflationary pressures in freight, lubricants, and coatings, though management currently deems the impact 'digestible.' Automotive demand in Europe remains a headwind, particularly in the premium segment, due to increased Chinese competition and lowered ambitions for battery electric vehicles. Working capital is expected to be a larger use of cash for the full year than previously anticipated, primarily due to the impact of higher metal prices. Direct exposure to Middle Eastern metal supply is limited to a small percentage of slabs and billets, which management believes can be resourced internally or externally.

Story Continues

Q&A Session Highlights

Sustainability of scrap spread benefits and second-half assumptions

Management confirmed that over 50% of scrap needs for the second half of 2026 are locked in, but the remainder remains open to market volatility. The guidance for 2026 assumes that favorable market conditions will continue throughout the year, marking an improvement over the negative impacts and tight scrap spreads experienced in the second half of 2024 and the first half of 2025.

Impact of Chinese EV manufacturers entering the European market

Management noted that new entrants like BYD utilize higher steel content in their vehicle bodies, limiting the immediate threat to Constellium's aluminum-heavy premium segment. The company remains focused on local-for-local production, which provides a buffer against global shipping disruptions.

Strategic shift toward increased scrap usage in production

Management clarified that while they are investing in 'upcycling' technologies, the goal is to lower metal costs by replacing primary metal with scrap rather than increasing total casting output. The ability to expand scrap usage is highly dependent on the real-time availability of specific scrap types and alloys in the market.
